statement: Let J = [t1, t2] lie in a compact classical time interval. Let 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1 be Lipschitz on J, vanish at its endpoints, and be extended by zero outside J. Let χ be a selected sum as in Lemma 6.2. One may integrate (6.5) labelwise against ψχ and a bounded C1 matrix Π(t), including Π = Id. More precisely, ∫ J ∫ ψχΠKt dy dv dt = B0 + ∫ J ∫ [ ψχΠ(R + A) + ψtχΠ fk0 r + ψχΠt fk0 r + ψΠ fDk0 rd χ′ s ] dy dv dt, (6.17) where the spatial integral has r = |X(t) − y| < t, all source quantities are evaluated at s = t − r, and B0 is the initial-cone boundary term. If ∥Π∥ ≲ 1, that boundary term is bounded in norm by C ∫ J |ψ(t0)| dt0. (6.18) 27 The constant in (6.18) depends only on the datum and fixed time horizon. For Π = Id, and for Π = wPX/|VX| when |VX| ≍ w, the derivative kernels satisfy the bounds above, uniformly in the fixed selected index set. For a general Π, its derivative term retains the explicit bound Cfθ∥Πt∥/(rϕ).
